regime_context: The detector shows a broad, two-horse leadership structure in Canada/TSX: Oil & Gas Producers holds the #1 rank with high durability (0.68) and high breadth (0.786) but is crowded (z 1.04), while Gold Miners sit as challenger with much lower breadth (0.267). Eight of sixteen themes are absolute-trend eligible, but the rotation flag is directional=false and one_narrative=false, implying no single dominant handoff is confirmed. Cross-sectional rank-IC is ~0 and rotation timing has no forward edge, so these are attention/focus leans only.
emerging_watch: Watching whether Pipelines & Midstream (unscorable, rank 6, eligible=true, durability 0.68, breadth 0.375) can close the gap on Oil & Gas as the energy leadership broadens beyond producers. The condition that retires this watch: a confirmed handoff where pipeline/midstream breadth and score exceed the Oil & Gas Producers theme for two consecutive weekly reads.

theses.subject: Oil & Gas Producers
theses.thesis: Oil & Gas is the #1-ranked eligible theme with the strongest durability (0.68) and broadest participation (0.786 breadth) — the only theme combining leadership with real market-wide breadth. Crowding (z 1.04) is a size-down caution, not a fade, and the absolute-trend gate (eligible=true) supports staying-power discipline rather than a return forecast.
theses.dissent: Crowding is elevated and breadth is historically high at the leader; if energy sentiment is already consensus, the marginal buyer is exhausted and a mean-reversion shakeout in XEG.TO could hit faster than the durability bar implies.

falsifier.text: XEG.TO lags the S&P/TSX by 5% or more while its breadth (fraction of constituents above trend) drops below 0.5 before the 20-day check-by date

theses.subject: Gold Miners
theses.thesis: Gold Miners sit as the #2-ranked challenger with a 0.502 margin behind Oil & Gas, eligible on the absolute-trend gate and not crowded (z 0.2). The theme is the only reasonable non-energy leadership candidate, but very narrow breadth (0.267) argues the move is concentrated in a few large names rather than a confirmed rotation.
theses.dissent: Breadth of 0.267 is poor — this is a handful of names carrying the theme, not a broad gold-mining tape; mixed hurst and weak durability (0.48) suggest the challenger could stall without confirmation.

falsifier.text: XGD.TO underperforms XEG.TO by 5% or its 30-day breadth stays below 0.35, showing the challenger never broadened out

theses.subject: Utilities & Renewables
theses.thesis: Utilities & Renewables is the highest-ranked INELIGIBLE (rank 8, score -0.115, eligible=false) theme, meaning the absolute-trend gate has turned off — the one validated risk-control leg says this theme is in a shake-out. The trend tag and negative crowding (z -0.78, uncrowded) do not override the gate.
theses.dissent: Utilities is a defensive rate-sensitive sector; if rates fall unexpectedly, XUT.TO could re-enter trend before the gate turns back on, and underweighting an uncrowded defensive theme could miss mean-reversion upside.

falsifier.text: XUT.TO re-enters its absolute-trend eligibility (price back above its trend filter) and the theme posts a positive 2-week return while the benchmark is flat or down

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
